title: Generic freeness for finitely presented algebra-module pairs
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative integral domain and $A$ a commutative $R$-algebra admitting a presentation $A\cong R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(g_1,\ldots,g_m)$ for finite $n,m\geq0$. Let $L$ be a finitely presented $A$-module [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. There is $0\ne a\in R$ such that $L_a$ is a free $R_a$-module, where $R_a=R[1/a]$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] and $L_a$ is the localized module [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away] of fractions $\ell/a^j$ with equality $\ell/a^j=\ell'/a^k$ if and only if some power of $a$ annihilates $a^k\ell-a^j\ell'$. Free means isomorphic to $\bigoplus_{i\in I}R_a$ for some set $I$, which need not be finite. No Noetherian hypothesis on $R$ is imposed.

proof.text: By [def-sc-finitely-presented-module], choose a presentation $L=A^{\oplus t}/\sum_{i=1}^s A n_i$. Put $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ and choose polynomial lifts $h_{ik}\in P$ of every coordinate of $n_i$. Thus, as an $R$-module, $L=P^{\oplus t}/W$, where $W$ is the $P$-submodule generated by $(h_{i1},\ldots,h_{it})$ and by all $g_j e_k$: quotienting first by the latter vectors gives $A^{\oplus t}$, and quotienting by the former gives exactly the chosen presentation of $L$.

Let $R_0\subseteq R$ be the unital subring generated by the finitely many coefficients of the $g_j$ and $h_{ik}$. It is a domain, since it is a subring of a domain. It is a finite-type $\mathbb Z$-algebra. The ring $\mathbb Z$ is Noetherian: any nonzero ideal is generated by its least positive element, since division with remainder leaves no smaller positive element in the ideal; the zero ideal is generated by $0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] to $\mathbb Z\to R_0$. Define $P_0=R_0[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, $B_0=P_0/(g_1,\ldots,g_m)$ and $M_0=B_0^{\oplus t}/\sum_i B_0 n_i^0$, using the coordinate vectors $h_{ik}$. The algebra $B_0$ is finite type over $R_0$, and $M_0$ is finite over $B_0$ because its $t$ coordinate vectors generate.

The coefficient-inclusion map $u:M_0\to L$ induces an $R$-linear map $\theta:R\otimes_{R_0}M_0\to L$, $r\otimes v\mapsto r u(v)$, by [lem-weil-pbc-module-base-change-universal-property]. It is an isomorphism, as follows directly from the presentations. For any $R$-module $N$, an $R_0$-linear map $M_0\to N$ is a family of images in $N$ for the monomial coordinate vectors $x^\alpha e_k$, subject to the relations given by all monomial multiples of $g_j e_k$ and $(h_{i1},\ldots,h_{it})$. An $R$-linear map $L\to N$ is the same family with exactly the same relations: every polynomial multiple is a finite linear combination of monomial multiples. All coefficients of the relations belong to $R_0$, so the two conditions coincide. Together with the cited scalar-extension bijection, restriction along $\theta$ is therefore bijective on maps into every $N$. Taking $N=R\otimes_{R_0}M_0$ gives a left inverse; taking $N=L$ and using injectivity of restriction shows it is also a right inverse. No flatness of $R$ over $R_0$ is used.

Apply [lem-pur-noetherian-algebra-module-generic-freeness] to $R_0\to B_0$ and $M_0$: step 2 verified all four hypotheses (Noetherian base, domain base, finite-type algebra, finite module). Obtain $a\in R_0\setminus\{0\}$ and a free $(R_0)_a$-module $(M_0)_a$. Regard $a$ as an element of $R$; it remains nonzero because $R_0\subseteq R$.

Put $H=R_a\otimes_{R_0}M_0$. Scalar extension of $u$ gives $H\to L_a$, $r\otimes v\mapsto r u(v)/1$, by [lem-weil-pbc-module-base-change-universal-property]. Write $\iota:R\otimes_{R_0}M_0\to H$ for the scalar-extension map $r\otimes v\mapsto (r/1)\otimes v$. An inverse to $H\to L_a$ is the fraction map $\ell/a^j\mapsto a^{-j}\iota(\theta^{-1}(\ell))$. This is well-defined: if $a^q(a^k\ell-a^j\ell')=0$, its image in $H$, where $a$ is invertible, implies $a^{-j}\iota(\theta^{-1}(\ell))=a^{-k}\iota(\theta^{-1}(\ell'))$. Addition and scalar multiplication follow by the module fraction formulas of [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. Both composites are the identity on fractions and on pure tensors, which generate their respective modules. Thus $L_a\cong H$.

There is an isomorphism $H\cong R_a\otimes_{(R_0)_a}(M_0)_a$. In one direction send $r\otimes v$ to $r\otimes(v/1)$. In the other send $r\otimes(v/a^j)$ to $(r/a^j)\otimes v$. The module fraction equality criterion of [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away] makes the second formula well-defined, since any annihilating power of $a$ becomes a unit in $R_a$; it is balanced over $(R_0)_a$ because multiplication of fractions gives $(c/a^k)(v/a^j)=cv/a^{k+j}$. The scalar-extension universal property [lem-weil-pbc-module-base-change-universal-property] gives the induced linear maps, and the two formulas compose to the identity. The map $(R_0)_a\to R_a$ is $c/a^j\mapsto c/a^j$, well-defined by [def-weil-ring-localization-away].

Choose a basis $(b_i)_{i\in I}$ of $(M_0)_a$ over $(R_0)_a$ from step 4. The explicit map $R_a\otimes_{(R_0)_a}(M_0)_a\to\bigoplus_{i\in I}R_a$ sends $r\otimes\sum_i c_i b_i$ to the finitely supported tuple $(r c_i)_i$; it is balanced, and its inverse sends a finitely supported tuple $(r_i)_i$ to $\sum_i r_i\otimes b_i$. The universal property [lem-weil-pbc-module-base-change-universal-property] supplies the linear extension, and the displayed formulas are mutually inverse. Steps 5 and 6 give $L_a\cong\bigoplus_{i\in I}R_a$, as required. Finite support, rather than finiteness of $I$, is all this argument needs.
